title: Superconductivity in Pb2-xBixPd Single Crystals
abstract: Chemical substitution provides an effective route to tune the structural and superconducting properties and to explore the evolution of superconductivity across related materials. In this work, we investigate the effect of Pb/Bi mixing on superconductivity in possible topological superconductors \ch{Pb2Pd} and $β$-\ch{Bi2Pd}, by synthesizing and characterizing single crystals of \ch{Pb_{2-x}Bi_{x}Pd} ($0.2\le x\le1.8$). Increasing Bi content triggers a structural phase transition from non-symmorphic ($I4/mcm$, $x<1$) to layered ($I4/mmm$, $x\ge1$) and induces a monotonic expansion of the lattice parameters. Across the doped range, all superconducting samples behave as weakly-coupled type-II superconductors exhibiting isotropic s-wave superconducting gaps.
summary: This work systematically studies the superconducting properties of $	ext{Pb}_{2-x}	ext{Bi}_x	ext{Pd}$ single crystals by varying the Pb/Bi ratio. The researchers found that doping causes a structural phase transition while maintaining weak-coupling, s-wave superconductivity. The comprehensive analysis uses multiple techniques to map out the superconducting phase diagram.
main_problem: The study investigates how chemical substitution of Pb with Bi affects the structural, superconducting, and topological properties of the $	ext{Pb}_2	ext{Pd}$ and $ eta-	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Pd}$ systems.
main_result: The doping induces a controlled structural phase transition, and all superconducting samples behave as weakly-coupled type-II superconductors with isotropic s-wave gaps.
method: The research combines single-crystal synthesis via the modified Bridgman technique with extensive characterization using XRD, magnetization (SQUID), resistivity, and specific heat measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{Pb}_{2-x}	ext{Bi}_x	ext{Pd}$ single crystal, studied across a doping range ($0.2 \le x \le 1.8$). Superconductivity is analyzed using models like the parallel resistor model and Ginzburg-Landau theory.
key_observables: Superconducting Transition Temperature ($T_c$), critical fields ($H_{C1}, H_{C2}$), superconducting volume fraction (SVF), and structural phase transition markers.
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($x$), lattice parameters, and the Ginzburg-Landau parameter ($\kappa_{GL}$), which increases with doping.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the parallel resistor model for resistivity fitting and uses standard superconducting models (GL equations) to characterize the phase.
figures_summary: Figures show crystal morphology changes (bulk vs. layered structure) based on doping, XRD patterns confirming crystal structure, and resistivity vs. temperature curves demonstrating the zero resistance drop.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: introduction of the doping concept, detailed characterization of structure (XRD/Laue), measurement of superconducting properties ($ho(T)$, $M(T)$, $C(T)$), and analysis using established superconducting models.
why_interesting: While primarily condensed matter, the study of tunable superconducting gaps and phase transitions in chemically substituted materials provides insights into pairing mechanisms relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.

FIG. 5. Superconducting phase diagram for the Pb2–xBixPd single crystals. The green, yellow, and blue markers indicate single-phase bulk superconductors, mixed-phase bulk super- conductors, and superconductors with volume fraction less than 2%, respectively. Circle, square, and triangle markers show TC from magnetization, resistivity, and specific heat, respectively. The green dotted line marks the transition in the crystal structure.
